prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1428; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Rear-end collision reported at a signalized intersection; insured vehicle was struck from behind while stopped, and the at-fault driver's carrier has been notified. Claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the scene photos and statements from two independent witnesses, who both describe the impact and sequence of events the same way the claimant and the other driver did. The vehicle damage to the rear bumper and trunk area is consistent with the described impact.

Entry 3: Confirmed the driver involved is listed on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of loss. No prior damage to the vehicle is on file, and nothing in the records points to earlier impact or pre-existing body damage to the vehicle.

Entry 4: Claimant's medical records were received showing a wrist fracture, which is a plausible injury for this type of impact. The treatment course followed a usual pattern and tapered as the claimant improved. A prior records check shows a minor strain in the same general area years ago that resolved fully with no lasting effects.

Entry 5: Claimant's attorney provided a written account that adds some small details not in the first recorded statement, though the core account of the collision has stayed consistent across all statements. Seating position in the vehicle at impact is not fully clear from the records and will be clarified in a follow-up interview.

Entry 6: Spoke with counsel to request the follow-up interview on seating position and to confirm the timeline of treatment. Counsel indicated the claimant will attend within the next two weeks and that updated treatment notes will be forwarded.

Entry 7: Reviewed the file with the injury evaluation and damage estimate in hand. Claim remains open pending the follow-up interview and receipt of updated treatment records, with no current indication of any coverage issue.
